_note: SAMPLE DATA for development only. Course codes and titles follow the calendar's style, but descriptions and prerequisite wording were written for this project and are not official. Replace by running fetch.py and build_data.py once scraping is approved.

courses.title: Computer Science Fundamentals I
courses.description: An introduction to programming and computational thinking using Python. Covers variables, control flow, functions, lists, files and basic problem solving. Designed for students with little or no programming experience.

courses.title: Computer Science Fundamentals II
courses.description: Continues introductory programming with object-oriented design in Java: classes, inheritance, recursion, linked lists, stacks, queues and a first look at algorithm analysis.
courses.prereq_text: Computer Science 1026A/B with a mark of at least 65%, or Engineering Science 1036A/B.

courses.title: Multimedia and Communications I
courses.description: An introduction to digital media: images, audio, video and web pages. Students build small interactive media projects. No programming experience required.

courses.title: Introduction to Computer Organization and Architecture
courses.description: How computers work below the programming language: data representation, digital logic, processor design, memory and assembly language programming.
courses.prereq_text: Computer Science 1027A/B.

courses.title: Applied Logic for Computer Science
courses.description: Propositional and predicate logic, proof techniques and their use in reasoning about programs, specifications and databases.
courses.prereq_text: Computer Science 1027A/B.

courses.title: Data Structures and Algorithms
courses.description: Design and analysis of fundamental data structures and algorithms: lists, trees, hash tables, priority queues, graphs, sorting and searching, with an emphasis on efficiency.
courses.prereq_text: Computer Science 1027A/B with a mark of at least 65%, and one of Mathematics 1600A/B or 1229A/B.

courses.title: Software Tools and Systems Programming
courses.description: Programming in C and working in a Unix environment: the shell, scripting, memory management, build tools, debugging and version control.
courses.prereq_text: Computer Science 1027A/B.

courses.title: Introduction to Software Engineering
courses.description: Team-based software development: requirements, design, testing, project management and an introduction to agile methods, through a term-long group project.
courses.prereq_text: Computer Science 2210A/B and 2211A/B.

courses.title: Discrete Structures for Computing
courses.description: Sets, relations, functions, counting, induction, recurrences and graphs, with applications in computer science.
courses.prereq_text: Computer Science 1027A/B and Mathematics 1600A/B.

courses.title: Operating Systems
courses.description: Processes, threads, scheduling, concurrency, memory management, file systems and security in modern operating systems.
courses.prereq_text: Computer Science 2208A/B and Computer Science 2211A/B.

courses.title: Object-Oriented Design and Analysis
courses.description: Object-oriented analysis and design using UML and design patterns, applied in a large team software project.
courses.prereq_text: Computer Science 2212A/B.

courses.title: Databases I
courses.description: Relational databases: data modelling, SQL, normalization, transactions and building applications on top of a database.
courses.prereq_text: Computer Science 2210A/B, Computer Science 2211A/B, and Computer Science 2214A/B.

courses.title: Foundations of Computer Science I
courses.description: Formal languages, finite automata, regular expressions, context-free grammars and an introduction to computability.
courses.prereq_text: Computer Science 2209A/B and Computer Science 2214A/B.

courses.title: Analysis of Algorithms I
courses.description: Techniques for designing and analysing algorithms: divide and conquer, greedy methods, dynamic programming, graph algorithms and NP-completeness.
courses.prereq_text: Computer Science 2210A/B and Computer Science 2214A/B, or registration in the Honours Specialization in Computer Science.

courses.title: Organization of Programming Languages
courses.description: How programming languages are designed and implemented: syntax, semantics, types, functional and logic programming.
courses.prereq_text: Computer Science 2210A/B and Computer Science 2211A/B.

courses.title: Artificial Intelligence I
courses.description: Search, knowledge representation, reasoning under uncertainty and an introduction to machine learning and neural networks.
courses.prereq_text: Computer Science 2210A/B and one of Statistical Sciences 2141A/B, Statistical Sciences 2244A/B or Statistical Sciences 2857A/B.

courses.title: Computer Graphics I
courses.description: Rendering pipelines, transformations, shading, texture mapping and interactive 3D graphics programming.
courses.prereq_text: Computer Science 2210A/B and Mathematics 1600A/B.

courses.title: Computer Networks I
courses.description: Network architectures and protocols, the Internet protocol stack, routing, reliable transport and network programming.
courses.prereq_text: Computer Science 3305A/B.

courses.title: Databases II
courses.description: Database internals: storage, indexing, query processing and optimization, concurrency control and recovery.
courses.prereq_text: Computer Science 3319A/B.

courses.title: Artificial Intelligence II
courses.description: Machine learning methods including deep neural networks, probabilistic models and reinforcement learning, with practical projects.
courses.prereq_text: Computer Science 3346A/B.

courses.title: Specification and Design
courses.description: Formal and semi-formal methods for specifying and designing reliable software systems.
courses.prereq_text: Computer Science 3307A/B with a minimum mark of 60%.

courses.title: Game Engine Development
courses.description: How video game engines are built: game loops, rendering, physics, animation, audio and tools. Students design and build a small game in teams.
courses.prereq_text: Computer Science 3350A/B or Computer Science 3307A/B. Registration in third or fourth year.

courses.title: Data Science Concepts
courses.description: An introduction to data science for any student: collecting, cleaning, visualizing and interpreting data, with simple programming and spreadsheets.

courses.title: Introduction to Data Analysis
courses.description: Exploratory data analysis, data wrangling and visualization in Python, with an introduction to predictive models.
courses.prereq_text: One of Data Science 1000A/B or Computer Science 1026A/B, and Statistical Sciences 1024A/B.

courses.title: Introduction to Machine Learning
courses.description: Supervised and unsupervised machine learning: regression, classification, clustering, model evaluation and ethics of prediction.
courses.prereq_text: Data Science 2000A/B and Mathematics 1600A/B.

courses.title: Fundamental Concepts in Mathematics
courses.description: An introduction to mathematical reasoning and proof: sets, functions, number theory and induction.
courses.prereq_text: Mathematics 1600A/B or Calculus 1000A/B.

courses.title: Methods of Matrix Algebra
courses.description: Vectors, matrices, systems of linear equations and determinants, with applications in science, business and the social sciences.
courses.prereq_text: Ontario Secondary School MHF4U or MCV4U.

courses.title: Linear Algebra I
courses.description: Systems of linear equations, matrices, vector spaces, linear transformations, eigenvalues and eigenvectors, with an emphasis on proofs and geometry.
courses.prereq_text: One of Ontario Secondary School MCV4U, MHF4U, or Mathematics 1229A/B.

courses.title: Intermediate Linear Algebra I
courses.description: Abstract vector spaces, inner products, orthogonality, diagonalization and canonical forms.
courses.prereq_text: Mathematics 1600A/B and Mathematics 1120A/B, each with a minimum mark of 60%.

courses.title: Mathematical Structures
courses.description: Logic, sets, relations, functions, cardinality and an introduction to proof writing for mathematics and computer science.
courses.prereq_text: Mathematics 1600A/B or Mathematics 1120A/B.

courses.title: Calculus I
courses.description: Limits, derivatives and their applications, and an introduction to integration. The standard first calculus course.
courses.prereq_text: Ontario Secondary School MCV4U.

courses.title: Calculus II
courses.description: Techniques and applications of integration, sequences, series and an introduction to differential equations.
courses.prereq_text: Calculus 1000A/B or Calculus 1500A/B.

courses.title: Calculus I for the Mathematical Sciences
courses.description: A more rigorous first calculus course for students planning to study mathematics, statistics or physics.
courses.prereq_text: Ontario Secondary School MCV4U with a mark of at least 85%.

courses.title: Calculus II for the Mathematical Sciences
courses.description: Integration, series and an introduction to multivariable calculus, taught with more theory than Calculus 1301A/B.
courses.prereq_text: Calculus 1500A/B or Calculus 1000A/B with a minimum mark of 85%.

courses.title: Advanced Calculus I
courses.description: Functions of several variables, partial derivatives, multiple integrals and vector calculus.
courses.prereq_text: Calculus 1501A/B or Calculus 1301A/B with a minimum mark of 85%, and Mathematics 1600A/B.

courses.title: Introduction to Statistics
courses.description: An intro statistics course: describing data, probability, sampling, confidence intervals and hypothesis tests, with everyday examples.

courses.title: Applied Probability and Statistics for Engineers
courses.description: Probability models, random variables, estimation, hypothesis testing and regression for engineering problems.
courses.prereq_text: Calculus 1301A/B or Calculus 1501A/B.

courses.title: Statistics for Science
courses.description: Statistical methods for science students: experimental design, t-tests, analysis of variance, regression and the use of statistical software.
courses.prereq_text: Statistical Sciences 1024A/B or Calculus 1000A/B or Mathematics 1229A/B.

courses.title: Probability and Statistics I
courses.description: Probability theory, discrete and continuous distributions, expectation and the central limit theorem.
courses.prereq_text: Calculus 1301A/B or Calculus 1501A/B (each with a minimum mark of 60%), or permission of the Department.

courses.title: Probability and Statistics II
courses.description: Estimation, likelihood, confidence intervals and hypothesis testing, building on Probability and Statistics I.
courses.prereq_text: Statistical Sciences 2857A/B.

courses.title: Introductory Physics I
courses.description: Mechanics for science students: motion, forces, energy, momentum and rotation, with laboratory work.
courses.prereq_text: Ontario Secondary School SPH4U and MCV4U.

courses.title: Introductory Physics II
courses.description: Electricity, magnetism, waves and optics, continuing Introductory Physics I.
courses.prereq_text: Physics 1501A/B.

courses.title: Discovering Chemical Structure and Bonding
courses.description: Atoms, molecules and the forces that hold them together: atomic structure, bonding, molecular shape and intermolecular forces.
courses.prereq_text: Ontario Secondary School SCH4U and MCR3U.

courses.title: Discovering Chemical Energetics and Reactivity
courses.description: Thermodynamics, equilibrium, acids and bases, kinetics and electrochemistry.
courses.prereq_text: Chemistry 1301A/B.

courses.title: Organic Chemistry for Life Sciences
courses.description: The structure and reactions of organic molecules, with examples from biology and medicine.
courses.prereq_text: Chemistry 1301A/B and Chemistry 1302A/B, each with a mark of at least 60%.

courses.title: Biology for Science I
courses.description: Cells, genetics, evolution and the diversity of life, with laboratory work.
courses.prereq_text: Ontario Secondary School SBI4U and SCH4U.

courses.title: Biology for Science II
courses.description: Physiology, ecology and how organisms interact with their environment.
courses.prereq_text: Biology 1001A or Biology 1201A.

courses.title: Scientific Methods in Biology
courses.description: How biological research is done: designing experiments, analysing data and communicating results.
courses.prereq_text: Biology 1001A and Biology 1002B, and Chemistry 1301A/B.

courses.title: Cell Biology
courses.description: The structure and function of cells: membranes, organelles, signalling and the cell cycle.
courses.prereq_text: Biology 1001A and Biology 1002B, and Chemistry 1301A/B and 1302A/B.

courses.title: Ecology
courses.description: Populations, communities and ecosystems, and how organisms interact with their environment.
courses.prereq_text: Biology 1001A and Biology 1002B.

courses.title: Genetics
courses.description: Inheritance, gene structure and expression, mutation and modern genetic techniques.
courses.prereq_text: Biology 1001A and Biology 1002B, and registration in a Science module.

courses.title: Introduction to Psychology
courses.description: An intro psychology course covering the science of behaviour and mind: the brain, perception, learning, memory, development, personality and mental health.

courses.title: Understanding Yourself and Others
courses.description: Applying psychology to everyday life: self-concept, relationships, stress, coping and wellbeing.
courses.prereq_text: Psychology 1002A/B.

courses.title: Child Development
courses.description: Physical, cognitive, social and emotional development from conception through childhood.
courses.prereq_text: Psychology 1002A/B with a mark of at least 60%.

courses.title: Introduction to Behavioural and Cognitive Neuroscience
courses.description: How the brain produces behaviour and thought: neurons, brain systems, sensation, emotion and memory.
courses.prereq_text: Psychology 1002A/B.

courses.title: Research Methods in Psychology
courses.description: How psychologists design studies, collect data and write research reports, with hands-on projects.
courses.prereq_text: Psychology 1002A/B, and registration in an Honours Specialization or Major in Psychology.

courses.title: Statistics for Psychology
courses.description: Statistics for psychology students: descriptive statistics, probability, hypothesis testing, correlation and analysis of variance.
courses.prereq_text: Psychology 1002A/B.

courses.title: Psychology of Learning
courses.description: How humans and animals learn: conditioning, reinforcement, memory and the biology of learning.
courses.prereq_text: Psychology 2810 and Psychology 2220A/B.

courses.title: Clinical Psychology
courses.description: An introduction to psychological disorders, assessment and evidence-based treatment.
courses.prereq_text: Psychology 2035A/B and Psychology 2810, or permission of the instructor.

courses.title: Principles of Microeconomics
courses.description: How individuals and firms make choices: supply and demand, markets, competition, monopoly and government policy.

courses.title: Principles of Macroeconomics
courses.description: The economy as a whole: output, unemployment, inflation, money, interest rates and government policy.

courses.title: Econometrics I
courses.description: Using statistics to test economic ideas: regression, inference and working with real economic data.
courses.prereq_text: Statistical Sciences 2244A/B or Statistical Sciences 1024A/B, Economics 1021A/B and Economics 1022A/B.

courses.title: Intermediate Microeconomic Theory I
courses.description: Consumer and producer theory, markets and welfare, using calculus-based models.
courses.prereq_text: Economics 1021A/B and Economics 1022A/B, and one of Mathematics 1229A/B, Calculus 1000A/B or Calculus 1500A/B.

courses.title: Intermediate Macroeconomic Theory I
courses.description: Models of economic growth, business cycles, and monetary and fiscal policy.
courses.prereq_text: Economics 1021A/B and 1022A/B, with a mark of at least 60% in each.

courses.title: Introduction to Business
courses.description: An overview of how businesses work: strategy, marketing, finance, operations and leadership, taught through cases.

courses.title: Accounting and Business Analysis
courses.description: Financial and managerial accounting: reading financial statements, costing, budgeting and using accounting information to make decisions.
courses.prereq_text: Business Administration 1220E, or Economics 1021A/B and Economics 1022A/B.

courses.title: Understanding Literature Today
courses.description: How to read and write about poetry, fiction, drama and film, from Shakespeare to the present.

courses.title: Enriched Introduction to English Literature
courses.description: An enriched introduction to literature for students with a strong background in English, from medieval texts to contemporary writing.
courses.prereq_text: Ontario Secondary School ENG4U with a mark of at least 85%.

courses.title: Children's Literature
courses.description: Stories written for children, from fairy tales to modern picture books and young adult fiction.
courses.prereq_text: At least 60% in English 1020 or 1022E, or permission of the Department.

courses.title: The Art of Writing
courses.description: Clear, persuasive writing for university: planning, drafting, revising and editing essays.

courses.title: Professional Writing
courses.description: Writing for the workplace: reports, proposals, emails and documents for different audiences.
courses.prereq_text: Writing 1000F/G or any first-year English course.

courses.title: Introduction to Philosophy
courses.description: An intro philosophy course: knowledge, mind, free will, ethics and the meaning of life.

courses.title: Introduction to Logic
courses.description: Formal logic: arguments, truth tables, natural deduction and predicate logic.

courses.title: Media Ethics
courses.description: Ethical questions raised by journalism, advertising, social media and entertainment.

courses.title: Introduction to Sociology
courses.description: How society shapes people: culture, groups, inequality, institutions and social change.

courses.title: Introduction to Social Statistics
courses.description: Statistics for social science research: describing data, probability, sampling and hypothesis testing.
courses.prereq_text: Sociology 1020.

courses.title: Introduction to Modern World History
courses.description: Major events and ideas that shaped the modern world, from the 1700s to today.

courses.title: Canada in the World
courses.description: Canada's place in world affairs from Confederation to the present.
courses.prereq_text: 1.0 History course at the 1000 level.

courses.title: Environment and Sustainability
courses.description: Environmental problems such as climate change, water and food, and how societies respond to them.

courses.title: Foundations of Geographic Information Science
courses.description: Maps, spatial data and an introduction to geographic information systems (GIS).
courses.prereq_text: Geography 1500F/G or registration in a Geography module.

courses.title: Programming Fundamentals for Engineers
courses.description: Programming for engineering students using Python: problem solving, functions, data structures and engineering applications.
courses.prereq_text: Registration in first-year Engineering.

courses.title: Algorithms and Data Structures for Object-Oriented Design
courses.description: Data structures and algorithms in an object-oriented setting, for software engineering students.
courses.prereq_text: Engineering Science 1036A/B, and registration in Software Engineering.

courses.title: Software Construction
courses.description: Building reliable software: design principles, testing, refactoring, version control and code review.
courses.prereq_text: Software Engineering 2205A/B or Computer Science 2210A/B.

courses.title: Introduction to Media Studies
courses.description: How media shape culture, identity and power, from print to streaming and social media.

courses.title: Video Games and Culture
courses.description: Video games as culture and art: game design, play, players, industry and representation.
courses.prereq_text: Media, Information and Technoculture 1020E.
